title: Naturalist reacts: elephant bath time
storyboard: Film: naturalist at a desk reacting to the clip, pointing at the ears on screen, 2 takes

scenes.headline: Elephant bath time. What's going on?
Big ears work like radiators
scenes.body: Flapping cools the blood in the ear veins and can lower body temperature by several degrees.

scenes.headline: Next trick: dirt and mud as sunscreen
scenes.body: It protects the skin from sun and bugs.

scenes.headline: Filmed at Pinnawala orphanage, Sri Lanka
scenes.body: A managed orphanage herd in the Maha Oya river, not a wild herd.

caption:
Why do elephants bathe so much?

Asian elephants in the wild drink about 189 litres (50 gallons) of water a day and eat 74-150 kg of food.

Source: Smithsonian's National Zoo.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
